title: Business Insights: SaaS usage and spend, workplace utilization, prerequisites and data sources

prose.label: Data sources.
prose.text: {{data-sources}} The fourth source is not named {{gap:fourth-source}}. {{usage-inputs}} {{subscribed-vs-used}} {{discovery-scale}}
The API is in [[business-insights.api]]; the separate Z-Insights analytics API is in [[shared.analytics.graphql]].

checks.do: Whether the tenant has Internet & SaaS, and for workplace insights Client Connector on the endpoints to be tracked.

purpose.statement: Business Insights gives visibility into an organization's SaaS application usage and spending, along with workplace metrics.

quotes: Zscaler Business Insights provides 360-degree visibility into your organization's SaaS application usage and spending insights, along with workplace metrics to help you save money and manage your workplace efficiently.

saas-features.statement: For SaaS applications it offers instant discovery, engagement data (engagement ratio, spending trends, saving opportunities, inactive users, usage by department), Shadow IT spending, visibility of all applications including overlaps, and cost control.

quotes: Instant Discovery: Configure your applications and start viewing their metrics instantly.
Engagement Data: Glance into the application's engagement ratio, spending trends, saving opportunities, inactive user data, usage by department, etc.
Shadow IT: View and calculate spending on Shadow IT applications purchased by departments or users within your organization.
SaaS Visibility: Experience total visibility into your application landscape. View the list of all your applications in one place, including overlaps.
Cost Control: Reduce unnecessary and redundant application expenses.

license-example.statement: Usage data is meant to help renew the correct number of licenses; Zscaler's example is an organization that bought more Microsoft 365 licenses than required analyzing how many are actually used and then reducing the number during the renewal process.

quotes: you're equipped with accurate data to renew the correct number of licenses required by your organization.

For example, if an organization purchases more than the required number of Microsoft 365 licenses, the data for how many of the purchased licenses are actually being used can be analyzed with the help of Business Insights and, subsequently, reduce the number of licenses during the renewal process.

workplace-features.statement: For the workplace it shows days in the office versus hybrid versus remote and which departments come in most, predictive cost-saving models, hour-by-hour office utilization with weekly, monthly and quarterly data across office locations, and workplace and workforce metrics.

quotes: Workplace Insights: Optimize office overheads with details on what days workers spend in the office vs. hybrid vs. remote, as well as which departments come into the office most frequently.
Cost Control: Rich insights and predictive cost-saving models enable you to save money by optimizing workplace utilization.
Leverage hour-by-hour office utilization data, and access weekly, monthly, and quarterly workplace usage data across all your office locations
Workplace and Workforce Metrics: Stay informed of your workplace and workforce utilization with the help of graphs and metrics.

prerequisites.statement: SaaS app insights require an Internet & SaaS subscription; workplace insights also require Client Connector deployed on all the endpoints to be tracked for office utilization.

quotes: To gain SaaS app insights, you must be subscribed to the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) service.
To gain workplace insights, in addition to the Internet & SaaS service, you must have Zscaler Client Connector deployed on all relevant endpoints you want to track for office utilization.

data-sources.statement: Business Insights receives signals from 4 data sources; the architecture article names Internet & SaaS, identity providers such as Okta and Entra ID, and SaaS application connector integrations (for apps such as Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google and GitHub).

quotes: Business Insights receives signals and data from 4 data sources: the Internet & SaaS service that acts as one of the input feeders, identity providers (IdPs) like Okta and Entra ID,
and SaaS application connector integrations (supported for apps such as Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google, and GitHub).

usage-inputs.statement: Business Insights presents app usage and workplace data by analyzing Internet & SaaS traffic, identity provider login data, or API integrations (direct app connectors).

quotes: presents the app usage and workplace data by analyzing your Internet & SaaS traffic, identity provider (login data), or API integrations (direct app connectors)

subscribed-vs-used.statement: It distinguishes subscribed apps from used apps through metadata fields for subscription details such as cost, license plans and contract start and end dates, all of which can be filtered for reports.

quotes: Business Insights can differentiate between your subscribed apps vs. used apps by populating metadata fields that show subscription details, such as cost, license plans, contract start dates, end dates, etc.
All of these fields can be filtered to present a report of representative apps.

discovery-scale.statement: Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps, but by default the portal shows only a subset chosen by business relevance.

quotes: Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps. By default, only a subset of these apps are shown in the portal, depending on your business relevance

fourth-source.title: The fourth Business Insights data source
fourth-source.detail: The architecture article says Business Insights has 4 data sources but names three. Unverified legacy statement: the fourth is custom application signatures. The custom applications API defines host signatures for apps, but no source calls them a data source.
fourth-source.blocks: listing everything that feeds Business Insights
